summary: "Top Secret" is a storytelling project featuring a leaked classified document concept that explains the purposes, operations, and ultimate fates of specific spacecraft. This project was designed to offer a fresh perspective, particularly to high school students who are curious about space.
details:
Project Overview & Objectives ("Abandoned but not Forgotten")

Core Objectives & Concept Elements

  • Leaked Document Concept: By presenting materials in the form of "Top Secret" stamped reports, the project creates a sense of solving a mystery for high school students, offering an immersive discovery experience rather than an ordinary scientific narrative.
  • Secret Fates of Spacecraft: It examines the original launch purposes, operational details, and post-mission abandonment processes of specific spacecraft and modules as "classified operational reports."
  • Designed for High School Students: It blends complex space pollution and aerospace history with a modern, interactive, and curiosity-driven language that young people can easily relate to.
  • Archaeological and Environmental Awareness: It demonstrates through evidence that the hardware left behind on the Moon and Mars is not merely "waste," but rather humanity's first archaeological artifacts in space and a silent environmental warning.

Data Sources & Methodology

To ensure scientific accuracy, our research utilized official NASA open source data, datasets, and archival photographs.

Development & Team Effort

We only used AI(Gemini) to translate a single text from Turkish to English. All other components of the project including concept design, research, structuring, and digital assembly using Canva are entirely our own work and dedication.

Video Production

For our project video, we used ChatGPT generated visuals and assembled and animated them into a cohesive video format entirely within Canva ourselves.

Impact & Vision

Aiming particularly to inspire and engage high school students, our project raises essential awareness about space sustainability, environmental ethics, and responsible future missions by highlighting the physical legacy of space exploration.
